passFindings: THE SHARPEST EXPRESSION OF RING GEOMETRY YET: rootkin's the_root_road travels 'only where life runs unbroken' and 'CANNOT CROSS THE DEAD OR THE MADE'; ashwarden's the_grey_road travels only where 'death has been SUBSTANTIAL AND RECENT'. Two travel crafts with MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE terrain, each walled off by exactly what the other owns. Nobody had to design this into the mechanics — it was already in the prose of both traditions.

MATCHED FUNCTION, OPPOSITE PHILOSOPHY, repeatedly: lifesense reads VIGOR / deathsense reads ENDING (both all-HARD bounds carrying their tradition's epistemic conscience); staunch BUYS TIME on a wound / the_kept_breath HOLDS A THRESHOLD (one refuses the death, the other endures alongside it); the_last_gift gives a dying person a good hour / the_cut_thread ends a living one instantly. The antipode pair is not opposition — it is the same questions answered differently.

TWO CAPSTONES REFUSING INTENSITY ON MORAL GROUNDS, not energetic ones: rootkin's the_last_gift ('there is no version of this that is not a decision about someone else's ending') and ashwarden's the_cut_thread. The catalog has now produced a category of bound I did not anticipate — the ETHICAL refusal, distinct from 'it costs too much to halve'.

CCODE — INTENSITY MAY NEED TO BE PER-RANK: draw_down conserves and surges normally at r1/r2, but its own r3 text says 'there is no partial version of this rank'. That is the first craft in the catalog where intensity availability CHANGES BY RANK rather than being a property of the whole craft.

wither's 'LIVING FLESH IS OUTSIDE IT AT EVERY RANK' is the catalog pre-empting the mastery question directly — the author wrote 'at every rank' precisely so no amount of practice would turn a decay-craft on a person. Strong support for the HARD/SOFT classing being real authorial intent rather than my imposition.

palework is the ContradictedByItsOwnTag craft (harmRung: lethal vs text denying killing). Per Erik's no-harm reversal, 'cannot kill the healthy' is classed SOFT — the tag wins. But 'cannot bring back' and 'the easing is a mercy, refusable' stay HARD: the reversal is about lethality, not about resurrection or consent.

A FOURTH cross-tradition reference: bark_and_briar's 'FIRE IS ITS PARTICULAR ENEMY' names blazeborn/radiant as the counter to rootkin's guard. The cross-tradition web now spans radiant↔harmonic (ranked soak), lattice↔churnfolk (order/chaos at scale), rootkin↔ashwarden (life/death terrain), and rootkin↔the light traditions (fire vs living ward).
